sources.scope: Only actual fixed-reference recursion nonaccumulation and finite bounded-horizon indices. No global physical-time path existence/uniqueness/measurability, Markov/invariance/kernel/hypocoercivity, PBPS main accuracy/implementation error/expected queries or PBPS-SPHMC composition. Author direct Exp mean-one SLLN remains an alternative open route; ASTIS uses verified bounded-indicator divergence. No merged/stabilized/purified/live/full-paper/Goal credit.

assumptions: E is finite-dimensional real inner-product with its Borel measurable structure; no positive-dimension restriction. V is C² and α,β≥0.
The six exact source conditions are α>0; α≤β; V∈C²; for all x,v, α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖²; η>0; βη≤1. No third or higher derivative condition.

y,xRef,z0 are arbitrary deterministic parameters. P and ε are literal canonical definitions. No probability, iid, positivity, divergence, cap, energy, waiting-time or recurrence certificate is a public premise.

Threshold positivity and faithful clamp/raw equality hold simultaneously only almost surely. The all-finite-horizon conclusion is pathwise on the common good-input event for each fixed parameter triple; no uncountable intersection over triples is assumed.

Stopped records have eventTime=∞ with no phase at infinity. The statement counts indices including index0, not a physical bounce-count expectation. The author direct Exp mean-one strong-law route is distinct from the reused ASTIS bounded-indicator sufficient route.
units.statement: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space, including dimension zero, with its Borel measurable structure. Let V:E→ℝ be C². Let α,β be nonnegative reals and η a real number satisfying α>0, α≤β, α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖² for every x,v∈E, η>0, and βη≤1. Fix any y,xRef∈E and initial phase z0=(x0,p0)∈E×E. Set c=y−η∇V(xRef). For z=(x,p), define the actual harmonic flow Φ_t(z)=(c+cos(t)(x−c)+√η sin(t)p, −sin(t)(x−c)/√η+cos(t)p), reflection S(z)=(x,p−[2〈p,g(x)〉/‖g(x)‖²]g(x)), residual g(x)=∇V(x)−∇V(xRef), and rate λ(z)=√η max{0,〈p,g(x)〉}. The reflection uses total real division, hence is the identity when g(x)=0. Define Λ(z,t)=∫_0^t λ(Φ_s(z)) ds for finite t≥0 and τ(z,e)=inf{t≥0:Λ(z,t)≥e}, with inf empty=∞. Let P be the actual countable product of rate-one exponential Borel measures on Ω=ℝ^ℕ; let ε_k(sample)=max{sample_k,0} viewed as a nonnegative real. Define active records (T,z) and an absorbing stopped record carrying no phase. Initialize record0=(0,z0). At index k, a stopped record stays stopped; an active record (T,z) becomes stopped if τ(z,ε_k)=∞ and otherwise becomes (T+τ(z,ε_k), S(Φ_{τ(z,ε_k)}(z))). Its event time T_k is the finite time component if active and ∞ if stopped. Then for these fixed y,xRef,z0, for P-almost every sample, simultaneously: (i) for every finite nonnegative horizon t, all sufficiently large k satisfy t<T_k; (ii) for every such t the set {k∈ℕ:T_k≤t} is finite. Initialization index0 is included, and ε_k is source E_(k+1). The result includes both eventual stopping and infinite continuing paths with unbounded event times; it does not assert eventual stopping. It is an actual-input, fixed-reference nonaccumulation conclusion of Appendix A.1 Ex9, with ASTIS total-record and finite-index adapters. The global physical-time process and its additional properties are separate obligations.
units.formula: P=\mathrm{Exp}(1)^{\otimes\mathbb N},\quad\varepsilon_k=\max\{\omega_k,0\},\quad P\text{-a.s.}:\ \forall t<\infty,\quad T_n>t\text{ eventually},\quad\#\{n:T_n\le t\}<\infty.

steps.title: Fix the actual source objects and stopped event times
steps.text: Use the literal harmonic flow, zero-safe reflection, integrated rate, first hitting time and stopped recursion from the actual finite-prefix theorem. Fix the canonical Exp1 product and its total nonnegative thresholds. The energy H and finite cap C are internal formulas: H(z)=(η⁻¹‖x−c‖²+‖p‖²)/2 and C=√η β√(2H(z0))(√(2ηH(z0))+‖c−xRef‖). They are proved recurrence invariants and bounds, not theorem assumptions.
steps.lean:
classical
  let P : Measure (ℕ → ℝ) := Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ => expMeasure (1 : ℝ))
  let ε : (ℕ → ℝ) → ℕ → ℝ≥0 := fun sample k => Real.toNNReal (sample k)
  let c : E → E → E := fun y xRef => y - η • gradient V xRef
  let Φ : E → E → ℝ → (E × E) → (E × E) := fun y xRef t z =>
    (c y xRef + Real.cos t • (z.1 - c y xRef) +
        (Real.sqrt η * Real.sin t) • z.2,
     (-Real.sin t / Real.sqrt η) • (z.1 - c y xRef) + Real.cos t • z.2)
  let S : E → (E × E) → (E × E) := fun xRef z =>
    (z.1, z.2 - (2 * inner ℝ z.2 (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef) /
      ‖gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef‖ ^ 2) • (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef))
  let rate : E → (E × E) → ℝ := fun xRef z =>
    Real.sqrt η * max 0 (inner ℝ z.2 (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef))
  let H : E → E → (E × E) → ℝ := fun y xRef z =>
    (η⁻¹ * ‖z.1 - c y xRef‖ ^ 2 + ‖z.2‖ ^ 2) / 2
  let C : E → E → (E × E) → ℝ := fun y xRef z =>
    Real.sqrt η * (β : ℝ) * Real.sqrt (2 * H y xRef z) *
      (Real.sqrt (2 * η * H y xRef z) + ‖c y xRef - xRef‖)
  let Λ : E → E → (E × E) → ℝ≥0 → ℝ := fun y xRef z t =>
    ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..(t : ℝ), rate xRef (Φ y xRef s z)
  let τ : E → E → (E × E) → ℝ≥0 → WithTop ℝ≥0 := fun y xRef z e =>
    MeasureTheory.hittingAfter
      (fun t : ℝ≥0 => fun a : (E × E) × (E × E) × ℝ≥0 =>
        Λ a.1.1 a.1.2 a.2.1 t - (a.2.2 : ℝ))
      (Set.Ici (0 : ℝ)) 0 ((y, xRef), z, e)
  let next : E → E → ℝ≥0 → ((ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit) →
      ((ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit) := fun y xRef e r =>
    match r with
    | Sum.inr _ => Sum.inr ()
    | Sum.inl a =>
      if τ y xRef a.2 e = ⊤ then Sum.inr () else
        Sum.inl (a.1 + (τ y xRef a.2 e).untopD 0,
          S xRef (Φ y xRef (((τ y xRef a.2 e).untopD 0 : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) a.2))
  let record : E → E → (E × E) → (ℕ → ℝ≥0) → ℕ →
      ((ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit) := fun y xRef z₀ e n =>
    Nat.rec (Sum.inl (0, z₀)) (fun k r => next y xRef (e k) r) n
  let eventTime : E → E → (E × E) → (ℕ → ℝ≥0) → ℕ → WithTop ℝ≥0 :=
    fun y xRef z₀ e n => (record y xRef z₀ e n).elim
      (fun a => (a.1 : WithTop ℝ≥0)) (fun _ => ⊤)
  change ∀ y xRef : E, ∀ z₀ : E × E, ∀ᵐ sample ∂P,
    (∀ t : ℝ≥0, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (t : WithTop ℝ≥0) < eventTime y xRef z₀ (ε sample) n) ∧
    (∀ t : ℝ≥0, {n : ℕ | eventTime y xRef z₀ (ε sample) n ≤ (t : WithTop ℝ≥0)}.Finite)

steps.title: Join the two actual compiled parents
steps.text: Apply the finite-recursion theorem to the six analytic source hypotheses. It supplies initialization, monotone times, absorbing stopping, C≥0, the positive-cap increment and zero-cap stopping. Apply the concrete product theorem to obtain a common positive-threshold event and divergent partial sums, with no supplied stochastic witness.
steps.formula: C\ge0,\quad C>0\Longrightarrow T_n+\varepsilon_n/C\le T_{n+1},\quad C=0,\ \varepsilon_n>0\Longrightarrow\text{next active record stops}.
steps.lean:
-- Reuse the actual deterministic recurrence; no cap or recurrence is supplied.
  rcases ActualFiniteJumpRecursion.actual_fixed_reference_finite_jump_recursion
      hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη with
    ⟨hinit, _, _, _, _, htime, hstop, _, hcap, _⟩
  -- The good event supplies all positive thresholds and divergent actual sums.
  rcases AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.UnitExponentialProduct.unit_exponential_product_laws with
    ⟨_, _, _, hgood, hdiv⟩

steps.title: Intersect the two good-input events
steps.text: For arbitrary fixed y,xRef,z0, intersect the almost-sure all-coordinate positivity and divergent-sum events. Positivity makes every clamped ε_k strictly positive. Extract the cap laws for this actual sample; these facts remain internal to the proof.
steps.lean:
intro y xRef z₀
  filter_upwards [hgood, hdiv] with sample hpos hsum
  have hepos (k : ℕ) : 0 < ε sample k :=
    Real.toNNReal_pos.mpr (hpos k).1
  obtain ⟨hC, hinc, hzero⟩ := hcap y xRef z₀ (ε sample)
steps.detail: Exact contiguous compiled proof region; preceding local definitions and facts remain in scope.

steps.title: Handle zero cap by absorbing stopping
steps.text: Split on C=0. The initial record is active and ε0>0, so its first update stops. Absorption proves T_(1+k)=∞ for every k. Every finite horizon is therefore exceeded at all indices n≥1. This includes zero-energy and dimension-zero cases.
steps.lean:
have hescape : ∀ t : ℝ≥0, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (t : WithTop ℝ≥0) < eventTime y xRef z₀ (ε sample) n := by
    -- Zero cap forces the first positive-threshold update to stop; it absorbs.
    by_cases hC0 : C y xRef z₀ = 0
    · have hfirst : record y xRef z₀ (ε sample) 1 = Sum.inr () :=
        hzero hC0 0 (0, z₀) (hinit y xRef z₀ (ε sample)) (hepos 0)
      intro t
      filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop (1 : ℕ)] with n hn
      obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hn
      have hs : record y xRef z₀ (ε sample) (1 + k) = Sum.inr () :=
        hstop y xRef z₀ (ε sample) 1 k hfirst
      change (t : WithTop ℝ≥0) < (record y xRef z₀ (ε sample) (1 + k)).elim _ _
      rw [hs]
      exact WithTop.coe_lt_top t
steps.detail: Exact contiguous compiled proof region; preceding local definitions and facts remain in scope.

steps.title: Sum the actual positive-cap increments
steps.text: In the other branch C≥0 and C≠0 give C>0. Let cap=toNNReal(C), whose real coercion is C. Starting from S0=T0=0, apply the actual extended-valued increment inequality and induction: S_(n+1)/C=S_n/C+ε_n/C≤T_n+ε_n/C≤T_(n+1). The same inequality remains valid after stopping since times are top.
steps.lean:
-- Positive cap: inductively compare every actual clock with partial sums/C.
    · have hCp : 0 < C y xRef z₀ := lt_of_le_of_ne hC (Ne.symm hC0)
      let cap : ℝ≥0 := Real.toNNReal (C y xRef z₀)
      have hcapcoe : (cap : ℝ) = C y xRef z₀ := Real.coe_toNNReal _ hC
      have hcapPos : 0 < cap := Real.toNNReal_pos.mpr hCp
      have hbound (n : ℕ) :
          (((∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, ε sample k) / cap : ℝ≥0) : WithTop ℝ≥0) ≤
            eventTime y xRef z₀ (ε sample) n := by
        induction n with
        | zero => simpa using (htime y xRef z₀ (ε sample)).1.ge
        | succ n ih =>
          have hi := hinc hCp n
          have hterm : Real.toNNReal ((ε sample n : ℝ) / C y xRef z₀) =
              ε sample n / cap := by
            rw [Real.toNNReal_div (ε sample n).coe_nonneg, Real.toNNReal_coe]
          rw [hterm] at hi
          calc
            (((∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), ε sample k) / cap : ℝ≥0) : WithTop ℝ≥0)
                = (((∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, ε sample k) / cap : ℝ≥0) : WithTop ℝ≥0) +
                    ((ε sample n / cap : ℝ≥0) : WithTop ℝ≥0) := by
                      rw [Finset.sum_range_succ, add_div, WithTop.coe_add]
            _ ≤ eventTime y xRef z₀ (ε sample) n +
                    ((ε sample n / cap : ℝ≥0) : WithTop ℝ≥0) := add_le_add ih le_rfl
            _ ≤ eventTime y xRef z₀ (ε sample) (n + 1) := hi

steps.title: Use divergent inputs to escape every finite horizon
steps.text: For any finite t, divergence gives S_n>tC eventually. Because C>0 this implies S_n/C>t. Combine this strict finite inequality, lifted into WithTop NNReal, with the prefix lower bound. This proves finite-horizon escape without requiring eventual equality to infinity.
steps.lean:
intro t
      have hs : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
          (t : ℝ) * C y xRef z₀ < ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, (ε sample k : ℝ) :=
        hsum.eventually (eventually_gt_atTop ((t : ℝ) * C y xRef z₀))
      filter_upwards [hs] with n hn
      have ht : t < (∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, ε sample k) / cap := by
        apply (NNReal.coe_lt_coe).mp
        push_cast
        rw [hcapcoe]
        exact (lt_div_iff₀ hCp).mpr hn
      exact lt_of_lt_of_le (WithTop.coe_lt_coe.mpr ht) (hbound n)

steps.title: Turn escape into a finite index set
steps.text: For each t, choose N such that n≥N implies t<T_n. Any n with T_n≤t must satisfy n<N. The sublevel index set is therefore contained in the finite natural interval [0,N); index0 is retained. Assemble both almost-sure conclusions.
steps.lean:
refine ⟨hescape, ?_⟩
  -- The bounded-horizon index set is contained in a finite initial interval.
  intro t
  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := eventually_atTop.mp (hescape t)
  apply (Set.finite_Iio N).subset
  intro n hn
  exact lt_of_not_ge (fun hge => (not_lt_of_ge hn) (hN n hge))
